doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: Woody Herman's troubles and jazz's status in America
summary: Jazz honored abroad but not at home; Woody Herman's tax trouble and Sinatra's help.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And it’s funny, the whole world looks at jazz players and jazz music as a vital art form, as a very important art form of the last fifty or hundred years — not here. Now they’re just starting, sort of like coming around to it but not here. If Woody Herman had gone through his number like he did when he was dying and when the IRS was ready to wheel his bed out in the street and take his house from him, anywhere else in the world he’s a hero, he would have been a national hero. But not here. It’s rather sad.
I think that somebody bailed him out. I hate to mention his name because I can’t stand him.
Frank Sinatra bailed him out a little bit, helped him out you know.
I think he let everybody know it too.
